name: Tomato
description: A fruit that is commonly used as a vegetable in cooking and agriculture. It is botanically classified as a berry but is often considered a vegetable due to its culinary and agricultural uses.

events.title: Wild Tomatoes in the Andes
events.description: Hundreds of years ago, long before Europeans had set foot in the New World, tomatoes grew wild in the Andes of western South America. The indigenous people cultivated them, eventually bringing the plant northward through Central America and into Mexico. When the Spanish arrived in the early 16th century, they found the inhabitants growing a food crop called 'tomatl' in the native language.
events.time_period: long before Europeans had set foot in the New World

events.title: Tomato Seed Introduction to Spain
events.description: Tomato seeds were brought from Mexico to Spain by those early explorers.
sources: Tomato seeds were brought from Mexico to Spain by those early explorers.

events.title: Tomato Spread to Italy
events.description: From there the plant spread to Italy by the mid-1500s where it began to be incorporated into regional cuisine.
sources: From there the plant spread to Italy by the mid-1500s where it began to be incorporated into regional cuisine.

events.title: Tomato Cultivation in Europe
events.description: Over the following decades, tomato plants were cultivated throughout Europe, but primarily as an ornamental plant.
sources: Over the following decades, tomato plants were cultivated throughout Europe, but primarily as an ornamental plant.

events.title: Tomato's Alternate Names
events.description: Along the way, the tomato was known by a number of names, including wolf peach and gold apple. In France, it was called a love apple (pomme d'amour) and thought to be an aphrodisiac.
sources: Along the way, the tomato was known by a number of names, including wolf peach and gold apple. In France, it was called a love apple (pomme d'amour) and thought to be an aphrodisiac.

events.title: Tomato's Toxicity
events.description: Because the tomato was mistakenly considered to be poisonous by many, it was referred to as the "poison apple."
sources: Because the tomato was mistakenly considered to be poisonous by many, it was referred to as the "poison apple."

events.title: Tomato's Chemical Composition
events.description: It's a fact that the leaves, stems and roots of the tomato contain solanine, a neurotoxin, and thus should not be eaten. The tomato also is a relative of deadly nightshade (Atropa belladonna).
sources: It's a fact that the leaves, stems and roots of the tomato contain solanine, a neurotoxin, and thus should not be eaten. The tomato also is a relative of deadly nightshade (Atropa belladonna).

events.title: Tomato and Poisonous Nature
events.description: The apparent proof of the tomato's poisonous nature was based on a false assumption. While it was true that upper class Europeans did die after consuming tomatoes, the fault was not with the tomato but with the pewter dinnerware used. The high level of acidity in tomatoes leached lead from the pewter, and those wealthy enough to afford to dine on pewter dinnerware died from lead poisoning after consuming tomato-based dishes.

events.title: Tomato in Americas
events.description: In the early 1700s, the tomato returned to the Americas with European colonists. At that time it was still grown primarily as an ornamental plant in the northern colonies but grown for its fruit in southern regions. Its popularity continued to increase.

events.title: Thomas Jefferson and Tomatoes
events.description: Thomas Jefferson reportedly grew tomatoes in his vegetable garden at Monticello and enjoyed eating the fruit. It wasn't until the early 1900s that tomatoes' popularity became widespread throughout the United States.

events.title: Tomatoes as a Vegetable
events.description: Today, tomatoes are grown around the world and are a star of international cuisine. They are grown in home gardens and on commercial farms. They are eaten raw, served cooked in a variety of dishes and processed into products that line our supermarket shelves. Tomatoes are the most popular home-grown vegetable crop in the country. However, are tomatoes really a vegetable?
